subproblem.title: A curve that lifts continuously through a map with injective derivative has its velocity in the range of the derivative
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (x₀ : Rn n) (c : ℝ → Rn n) (γ : ℝ → Rn N) (v : Rn N), DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ x₀ → Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀) → Tendsto c (𝓝 (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 x₀) → (∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ), γ t = ψ (c t)) → HasDerivAt γ v 0 → v ∈ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀).toLinearMap
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 8–11 of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangentSpace_eq_range, i.e. the analytic core of Part B. There, steps 6–7 produce the lift c(t) and the factorisation γ(t) = ψ(c(t)); here they are hypotheses (iii) and (iv). Differentiability of c is neither assumed nor used.

Setting and notation. A := fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ and |·| denotes the Euclidean norms. By hypothesis (iv), fix τ > 0 with γ(t) = ψ(c(t)) for all |t| < τ.

Proof.
0. Base point.
(i) c(0) = x₀. Let U be any neighbourhood of x₀. By hypothesis (iii), c⁻¹(U) is a neighbourhood of 0, so it contains 0 and c(0) ∈ U. Since ℝⁿ is Hausdorff, c(0) = x₀.
(ii) Taking t = 0 in the factorisation gives γ(0) = ψ(c(0)) = ψ(x₀).
1. Differentiability. ψ is differentiable at x₀ with derivative A. Write e(x) := ψ(x) − ψ(x₀) − A(x − x₀). Then for every ε > 0 there is δ_ε > 0 with |e(x)| ≤ ε|x − x₀| whenever |x − x₀| < δ_ε.
2. Lower bound (parent step 8). A is injective and ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional, so there is λ > 0 with |Aζ| ≥ λ|ζ| for all ζ ∈ ℝⁿ. If n = 0, take λ = 1; then ζ = 0 always. Otherwise ζ ↦ |Aζ| is continuous and, by injectivity, positive on the compact nonempty unit sphere, so it has a positive minimum λ there. For ζ ≠ 0, apply this to ζ/|ζ|.
3. Bounded difference quotients (parent step 9). Since c(t) → x₀ as t → 0, there is τ₁ ∈ (0, τ] with |c(t) − x₀| < δ_{λ/2} for |t| < τ₁. For such t, use γ(t) = ψ(c(t)) and γ(0) = ψ(x₀), step 1 with ε = λ/2, and step 2:
|γ(t) − γ(0)| = |A(c(t) − x₀) + e(c(t))| ≥ λ|c(t) − x₀| − (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀| = (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀|.
Since γ has derivative v at 0, there is τ₂ ∈ (0, τ₁] with |γ(t) − γ(0) − t v| ≤ |t| for |t| < τ₂. Then |γ(t) − γ(0)| ≤ (|v| + 1)|t|, so (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀| ≤ (|v| + 1)|t| for |t| < τ₂. Hence ζ(t) := t⁻¹(c(t) − x₀) satisfies |ζ(t)| ≤ C := 2(|v| + 1)/λ for 0 < |t| < τ₂.
4. Compactness (parent step 10). Let t_j := τ₂/(j + 2) for j ∈ ℕ. Then 0 < t_j < τ₂, t_j → 0 and |ζ(t_j)| ≤ C. By Bolzano–Weierstrass in ℝⁿ, there is a strictly increasing sequence j_k such that s_k := t_{j_k} gives ζ(s_k) → ζ for some point ζ ∈ ℝⁿ. Still s_k ≠ 0 and s_k → 0.
5. Identification of the limit (parent step 11). For every k, 0 < s_k < τ, so γ(s_k) = ψ(c(s_k)) and
(γ(s_k) − γ(0))/s_k = (A(c(s_k) − x₀) + e(c(s_k)))/s_k = Aζ(s_k) + e(c(s_k))/s_k.
(a) The left side tends to v, because γ has derivative v at 0, s_k → 0 and s_k ≠ 0.
(b) Aζ(s_k) → Aζ, because A is linear on the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ, hence continuous.
(c) e(c(s_k))/s_k → 0. Let ε > 0. Since s_k → 0 and c(t) → x₀, we have c(s_k) → x₀, so |c(s_k) − x₀| < δ_ε for all large k. Then |e(c(s_k))/s_k| ≤ ε|c(s_k) − x₀|/|s_k| = ε|ζ(s_k)| ≤ εC.
By (a)–(c) and uniqueness of limits in ℝᴺ, v = Aζ. Hence v ∈ range A = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀).toLinearMap. This proves the theorem.

Remark: an alternative ending. Steps 0–5 already prove the theorem. A formalizer may replace steps 4–5 by the following equally complete argument.
(i) By step 1 composed with c(t) → x₀, e(c(t)) = o(|c(t) − x₀|) as t → 0.
(ii) Step 3 gives |c(t) − x₀| ≤ C|t| for |t| < τ₂ (trivially at t = 0), so c(t) − x₀ = O(t). Hence e(c(t)) = o(t), and t⁻¹e(c(t)) → 0 as t → 0.
(iii) For 0 < |t| < τ, A(t⁻¹(c(t) − x₀)) = t⁻¹(γ(t) − γ(0)) − t⁻¹e(c(t)). The first term tends to v along t → 0, t ≠ 0, because γ has derivative v at 0. So A(t⁻¹(c(t) − x₀)) → v along t → 0, t ≠ 0, a nontrivial filter on ℝ.
(iv) Every A(t⁻¹(c(t) − x₀)) lies in range A, a finite-dimensional and hence closed subspace of ℝᴺ. Therefore v lies in the closure of range A, which is range A itself.
This is the route used for the scratch Lean check.

proof_key_steps: c(0) = x₀ (unpunctured limit in a Hausdorff space) and γ(0) = ψ(x₀); the remainder e(x) = ψ(x) − ψ(x₀) − A(x − x₀) is o(|x − x₀|).
Injectivity of A on the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ gives λ > 0 with |Aζ| ≥ λ|ζ|.
Near 0, (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀| ≤ |γ(t) − γ(0)| ≤ (|v| + 1)|t|, so ζ(t) = (c(t) − x₀)/t is bounded by C = 2(|v| + 1)/λ.
Bolzano–Weierstrass along t_j = τ₂/(j + 2) gives s_k → 0, s_k ≠ 0, ζ(s_k) → ζ.
(γ(s_k) − γ(0))/s_k = Aζ(s_k) + e(c(s_k))/s_k tends both to v and to Aζ, so v = Aζ ∈ range A.

The supplied closed-range alternative is also complete. Neither argument assumes differentiability of c or uses the parent theorem.

subproblem.title: Range of the chart derivative lies in the tangent space (Simon 2.4.3, Part A)
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ and write ℝᵏ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k). Let M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ. Assume V is open, ψ is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V), and ψ maps V into M (MapsTo ψ V M). Then for every x ∈ V, the range of Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x is contained in tangentSpace M (ψ x). Here tangentSpace M y is the linear span of all vectors γ′(0) such that γ : ℝ → ℝᴺ is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, satisfies γ(0) = y and has derivative γ′(0) at 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → MapsTo ψ V M → ∀ x ∈ V, LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap ≤ tangentSpace M (ψ x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part A (steps 1–4) of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangentSpace_eq_range. This is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, 4.3, p. 55; the printed text only says 'one readily checks'. That argument uses only that V is open, ψ is C¹ on V and ψ maps V into M, so this child is stated under exactly these hypotheses. The parent obtains them from IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ and 1 ≤ r.

Setting and notation. |·| denotes the Euclidean norms. Fix x₀ ∈ V. Put y₀ := ψ(x₀) and A := Dψ(x₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀. Let G be the set of generators of tangentSpace M y₀: v ∈ G iff there is γ : ℝ → ℝᴺ that is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, has γ(0) = y₀ and has derivative v at 0. Thus tangentSpace M y₀ = span G is a linear subspace of ℝᴺ containing G. The claim LinearMap.range A ≤ tangentSpace M y₀ means: A w ∈ tangentSpace M y₀ for every w ∈ ℝⁿ.

Proof.
1. Differentiability. V is open and x₀ ∈ V, so V is a neighbourhood of x₀. ψ is C¹ on V, hence differentiable within V at x₀. Since V is a neighbourhood of x₀, ψ is differentiable at x₀, with Fréchet derivative A = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ at x₀.
2. Let w ∈ ℝⁿ. If w = 0, then A w = 0 ∈ tangentSpace M y₀, because a linear subspace contains 0. Now let w ≠ 0, so |w| > 0. Since V is open, choose ρ > 0 with B(x₀, ρ) ⊆ V, where B is the open ball. Put κ := ρ/(2|w|) > 0, ℓ(t) := x₀ + (κ t) w and γ(t) := ψ(ℓ(t)) for t ∈ ℝ.
3. Let t ∈ (−1,1). Then |ℓ(t) − x₀| = κ|t||w| = (ρ/2)|t| < ρ, so ℓ(t) ∈ B(x₀, ρ) ⊆ V. Hence γ(t) = ψ(ℓ(t)) ∈ M, because ψ maps V into M. Thus ℓ maps (−1,1) into V and γ maps (−1,1) into M. The map ℓ is affine, hence C^∞ and in particular C¹ on ℝ. ψ is C¹ on V and ℓ maps (−1,1) into V, so by the composition rule for C¹ maps on sets, γ = ψ ∘ ℓ is C¹ on (−1,1). Also ℓ(0) = x₀, so γ(0) = ψ(x₀) = y₀.
4. The map t ↦ x₀ + (κ t) w has derivative κ w at 0. By step 1, ψ has Fréchet derivative A at ℓ(0) = x₀. The chain rule shows that γ = ψ ∘ ℓ has derivative A(κ w) = κ·A w at 0, using linearity of A. Together with step 3, γ witnesses κ·A w ∈ G ⊆ tangentSpace M y₀. Since tangentSpace M y₀ is a linear subspace and κ ≠ 0, A w = κ⁻¹·(κ·A w) ∈ tangentSpace M y₀.
5. Conclusion. Steps 2–4 give A w ∈ tangentSpace M y₀ for every w ∈ ℝⁿ, i.e. LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀).toLinearMap ≤ tangentSpace M (ψ x₀). Since x₀ ∈ V was arbitrary, the theorem follows.

- Step 1: ContDiffOn.differentiableOn_one (Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Defs.lean:582), DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt with IsOpen.mem_nhds, DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt.
- Step 2: Metric.isOpen_iff, norm_pos_iff.
- Step 3: ContDiffOn.comp (Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Comp.lean:125) with ContDiff.contDiffOn, where contDiff_const.add ((contDiff_const.mul contDiff_id).smul contDiff_const) gives ContDiff ℝ 1 ℓ; MapsTo.comp.
- Step 4: HasDerivAt.const_mul, HasDerivAt.smul_const and HasDerivAt.const_add for ℓ; HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt (Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Comp.lean:374); unfold tangentSpace, then Submodule.subset_span (LinearAlgebra/Span/Defs.lean:75); map_smul, Submodule.smul_mem, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀.
proof_key_steps: ψ is C¹ on the open set V, so it is differentiable at x₀ with derivative A = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀.
For w = 0, Aw = 0 lies in the subspace. For w ≠ 0, choose B(x₀, ρ) ⊆ V and κ = ρ/(2|w|).
The curve γ(t) = ψ(x₀ + κ t w) is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into ψ(V) ⊆ M, and has γ(0) = ψ(x₀).
Chain rule: γ′(0) = κ·Aw, so κ·Aw is a generator. Dividing by κ gives Aw ∈ tangentSpace M (ψ x₀); hence range A ≤ tangentSpace M (ψ x₀).

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis and exactly matches the Lean proposition. Rescaled affine curves remain in V throughout (-1,1), their compositions are C¹ curves in M, and the chain rule gives velocity κ·Aw. Subspace closure and κ ≠ 0 recover Aw; w = 0 is handled separately. This proves the inclusion without any parent or sibling reliance.

subproblem.title: Tangent space lies in the range of the chart derivative, given a continuous chart inverse (Simon 2.4.3, Part B)
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, write ℝᵏ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), and let r ∈ ℕ∞ with 1 ≤ r. Let M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ satisfy IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V and W are open, ψ is C^r on V, ψ is injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(x) is injective for x ∈ V. Let g := Function.invFunOn ψ V : ℝᴺ → ℝⁿ; g(y) is a point of V mapped to y by ψ when such a point exists, and a fixed arbitrary point otherwise. Assume moreover that g is continuous on W ∩ M in the relative topology (ContinuousOn g (W ∩ M)). Then for every x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) ⊆ range Dψ(x), where Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x. Here tangentSpace M y is the linear span of all vectors γ′(0) such that γ : ℝ → ℝᴺ is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, satisfies γ(0) = y and has derivative γ′(0) at 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), 1 ≤ r → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ContinuousOn (Function.invFunOn ψ V) (W ∩ M) → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) ≤ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part B of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangentSpace_eq_range, namely steps 5–7 and the conclusion of step 11. The parent obtains continuity of ψ⁻¹ = invFunOn ψ V on W ∩ M from its sibling theorem chart_inverse_continuous; here it is a hypothesis. The analytic core (parent steps 8–11) is the sibling theorem lift_velocity (Submission.simon_lift_velocity_mem_range_fderiv).

Setting and notation. Fix x₀ ∈ V. Put y₀ := ψ(x₀), A := Dψ(x₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀, and T := range A, a linear subspace of ℝᴺ. Let G be the set of generators of tangentSpace M y₀: v ∈ G iff some γ : ℝ → ℝᴺ is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, has γ(0) = y₀ and has derivative v at 0. Thus tangentSpace M y₀ = span G. Note that y₀ ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M.

Proof.
1. Differentiability and injectivity at x₀. Since 1 ≤ r and ψ is C^r on V, ψ is C¹ on V; this needs the cast of (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ r to WithTop ℕ∞. V is open and x₀ ∈ V, so ψ is differentiable at x₀. By the last field of IsSimonLocalRepresentation, A = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀ is injective.
2. Reduction. T is a linear subspace and tangentSpace M y₀ = span G, so it suffices to show G ⊆ T. Let v ∈ G, witnessed by γ: γ is C¹ on (−1,1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = y₀, and γ has derivative v at 0.
3. γ stays in W ∩ M near 0 (parent step 6). γ is differentiable, hence continuous, at 0. Since γ(0) = y₀ ∈ W and W is open, γ(t) ∈ W for all t in some neighbourhood of 0. Also (−1,1) is a neighbourhood of 0, and γ(t) ∈ M for t ∈ (−1,1). Hence γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M for all t in some neighbourhood of 0.
4. The lift (parent step 7). Let g := Function.invFunOn ψ V and c(t) := g(γ(t)). Take t in the neighbourhood of step 3. Then γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), so some point of V is mapped to γ(t), and the defining property of invFunOn gives ψ(c(t)) = γ(t). Thus γ(t) = ψ(c(t)) for all t in a neighbourhood of 0.
5. Continuity of the lift at 0 (parent step 7). Since ψ is injective on V and x₀ ∈ V, g(ψ(x₀)) = x₀, i.e. g(y₀) = x₀. By hypothesis, g is continuous on W ∩ M, in particular continuous within W ∩ M at y₀ ∈ W ∩ M: g(y) → g(y₀) = x₀ as y → y₀ with y ∈ W ∩ M. Since γ is continuous at 0 with γ(0) = y₀, and γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M for t near 0 by step 3, γ tends to y₀ within W ∩ M as t → 0. Composing, c(t) = g(γ(t)) → x₀ as t → 0 along the full neighbourhood filter of 0. This is consistent with c(0) = g(y₀) = x₀.
6. Apply the sibling theorem lift_velocity (Submission.simon_lift_velocity_mem_range_fderiv) to ψ, x₀, c, γ, v. Its hypotheses hold: ψ is differentiable at x₀ and A is injective (step 1); c(t) → x₀ as t → 0 (step 5); γ(t) = ψ(c(t)) for t in a neighbourhood of 0 (step 4); γ has derivative v at 0 (step 2). It yields v ∈ range A = T.
7. Conclusion. Hence G ⊆ T, so tangentSpace M y₀ = span G ⊆ T, i.e. tangentSpace M (ψ x₀) ≤ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀).toLinearMap. Since x₀ ∈ V was arbitrary, the theorem follows.

proof_key_steps: 1 ≤ r and V open give differentiability of ψ at x₀, and A = Dψ(x₀) is injective.
By span_le it suffices to show that each generator v, the velocity at 0 of a C¹ curve γ in M with γ(0) = ψ(x₀), lies in range A.
γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, so γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M for t near 0.
c(t) := invFunOn ψ V (γ(t)) satisfies ψ(c(t)) = γ(t) near 0, and c(t) → x₀ by the continuity hypothesis and injectivity on V.
The sibling lift_velocity gives v ∈ range A; hence tangentSpace M (ψ x₀) ≤ range A.
